chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Shamun from Abdullah b. Sinan from al-Fudayl b. Yasar. He said:

I went to Zayd b. Ali (peace be upon him) on the morning that he set out in Kufa, and I heard him saying: Who among you will help me fight the Nabateans of the people of the Levant? For, by the One who sent Muhammad in truth as a bringer of good tidings, no one from you who helps me fight them except that I will take his hand on the Day of Resurrection and admit him into Paradise by the permission of God.

He said: So when he was killed, I hired a mount and headed toward Medina. I entered upon al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and I said to myself: I will not inform him about the killing of Zayd b. Ali, for he will become distressed over it. So when I entered upon him, he said to me: O Fudayl, what did my uncle Zayd do? He said: The tears choked me, so he said to me: Did they kill him? I said: Yes, by God, they killed him. He said: Did they crucify him? I said: Yes, by God, they crucified him. He said: So he began to weep, and his tears flowed down both cheeks of his face as if they were pearls.

Then he said: O Fudayl, did you join my uncle in fighting the people of the Levant? I said: Yes. He said: How many of them did you kill? I said: Six. He said: Perhaps you are in doubt about their blood? He said: And I said: If I were in doubt, I would not have killed them. He said: Then I heard him saying: May God make me a partner in that blood. By God, my uncle Zayd and his companions have passed away as martyrs, just like Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and his companions.

key_terms.أنباط أهل الشام: Nabateans of the Levant; derogatory term for the Umayyad forces from Syria
key_terms.الجمان: Pearls; metaphor for the Imam's tears, expressing profound grief
key_terms.شهداء: Martyrs; those who die fighting for a righteous cause
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection; the eschatological day of divine judgment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Zayd b. Ali's uprising and his martyrdom?
ai.summary: Al-Fudayl b. Yasar recalls visiting Zayd b. Ali on the morning of his uprising in Kufa, hearing his call to arms against the Umayyad forces. After Zayd's martyrdom, al-Fudayl travels to Medina where Imam al-Sadiq, despite not being told, miraculously knows of his uncle's fate and weeps. The Imam validates Zayd's cause, asking about al-Fudayl's participation and declaring Zayd and his companions martyrs equal to those of Imam Ali. This hadith affirms the legitimacy of Zayd's uprising and the Imamic family's solidarity.
